purpose: Documented, evidence-backed corrections applied to processed source tables. Original NASA PSI tables under integration_update/data/raw_psi_experimental_tables/ are never modified.
applied_by: src/apply_source_corrections.py (idempotent: a cell is changed only if it still holds the old value)

corrections.source_text: PSI-99 table prints '037 mm' (missing decimal point)
corrections.evidence: Ferkul, Olson, Urban, Ruff et al., 'Results of Large-Scale Spacecraft Flammability Tests', ICES-2017 (NTRS 20170008805): samples 2-4, 2-5 and 2-6 are 0.37 mm thick.
corrections.quality_flag: thickness_corrected: NASA PSI-99 prints '037 mm'; 0.37 mm per Ferkul et al. ICES-2017 (NTRS 20170008805)

corrections.source_text: PSI-98 table gives 0.37 under the header 'Sample Thickness (cm)'
corrections.evidence: Ferkul et al. ICES-2017 (NTRS 20170008805) states Saffire-II sample 2-5 is the same cotton-fiberglass fabric used in Saffire-I and is 0.37 mm thick. Jomaas et al. (Acta Astronautica preprint) gives the Saffire-1 SIBAL fuel as 0.3175 mm. A 3.7 mm cotton-fiberglass fabric is not consistent with any published description; the header unit (cm) is treated as a source error.
corrections.confidence: high; inferred from publications, header unit in NASA table conflicts
corrections.quality_flag: thickness_unit_corrected: NASA PSI-98 header says cm (0.37 cm = 3.7 mm); published SIBAL thickness is 0.32-0.37 mm, value set to 0.37 mm

corrections.evidence: NASA 'The Spacecraft Fire Experiment (Saffire) - Objectives, Development and Status' (NTRS 20170001636) lists SIBAL fabric as 0.33 mm thick; published SIBAL thickness is 0.32-0.37 mm. The 'cm' unit in the NASA table is treated as a source error.
corrections.confidence: high; inferred from publications, unit in NASA table conflicts
corrections.quality_flag: thickness_unit_corrected: NASA PSI-100 prints '.33 cm' (3.3 mm); published SIBAL thickness is 0.33 mm

not_corrected.note: PSI-99 table gives 20 cm/s; Ferkul et al. ICES-2017 gives 25 cm/s and NTRS 20170001636 gives 30 cm/s for the second SIBAL sample. Sources disagree, so the NASA table value (20 cm/s) is kept and flagged in docs.
This layer is a literal parse of the original NASA tables ('037 mm' -> 37 mm, '0.37' cm -> 3.7 mm) and is labelled unverified. It is left literal; use the corrected processed tables for analysis.
